description: Two guys who don't know what to do with themselves
summary:
AstroHealth is an interactive web application that demonstrates astronaut health monitoring during space missions. It combines a 3D spacesuit model, simulated measurements, and visual alerts to make health information easier to understand.

The website offers three views. In 3D Spacesuit, users can rotate a Gemini model and select sensors to check their locations and readings. Astronaut View provides a first-person perspective with Earth in the background and a wrist-mounted display. Mission Control shows all measurements on a virtual laptop dashboard.

The application monitors heart rate, oxygen saturation, body temperature, suit pressure, respiratory rate, and hydration. Body temperature appears only on the 3D model and mission control dashboard. Readings outside configured demonstration ranges trigger visual warnings.

Built with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Three.js, and Python, AstroHealth receives simulated telemetry from a local Python server or generates it directly in the browser.

The project demonstrates how clear interfaces can connect sensor locations with important measurements. It is an educational prototype, not a validated medical system. Future improvements could include real sensors, measurement history, trend charts, and NASA datasets.
details:
AstroHealth is an interactive web prototype that demonstrates astronaut health monitoring. Users can explore a rotating Gemini spacesuit, select sensors, check a wrist display from an astronaut’s perspective, and review measurements on a mission control dashboard.

It monitors six parameters: heart rate, oxygen saturation, body temperature, suit pressure, respiratory rate, and hydration. A local Python server supplies simulated telemetry through a JSON API, with browser-based simulation available as a fallback. JavaScript compares readings with configured demonstration ranges and displays visual warnings.

We developed AstroHealth using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Three.js, Python, and a GLB spacesuit model. The prototype runs in a browser without dedicated sensor hardware.

Its creative feature is presenting the same information through three connected perspectives: sensor locations on the suit, an astronaut’s wrist display, and the base dashboard. This makes abstract measurements more tangible.

We considered readability, sensor placement, navigation, information density, and operation without a server. The wrist display shows five parameters, while body temperature remains on the suit and base dashboard.

The intended impact is educational: helping users understand telemetry and how interface design supports awareness. It uses simulated data and is not a validated medical system. Future work could add real sensors and measurement history.
